August 19, 2026

Iran said to be preparing strikes on US bases in Europe as ultimatum expires

tags: war, politics, defence
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Iranian officials are preparing to go on the offensive as an ultimatum issued to the United States expires without concessions, according to the Financial Times and two senior officials in Tehran. IRGC officials are assessing strikes on US military assets in Cyprus and Bulgaria, with other locations potentially to follow. Tehran has cited US targeting of Iranian infrastructure as the justification. No strikes have taken place, and the plans could still be reversed.

Turkey condemns Israeli strike on Syrian base near its border

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Turkey criticised Israel following a strike on a Syrian military base close to the Turkish border. Separately, the United Arab Emirates suspended trade and financial ties with Iran after a new missile threat.

Israeli minister calls for nightly targeted killings in Gaza

tags: war, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir said targeted eliminations should be carried out in Gaza every night, describing a figure of 30 to 40 people. He said the targets should not be limited to those posing an immediate threat, adding that those people should not be alive.

Trump-endorsed candidates fall in primaries as Democrats nearly flip deep-red Pennsylvania seat

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

Three candidates endorsed by Donald Trump lost primary races, two in Florida and one in Wyoming, bringing the number of his endorsed candidates defeated this primary season to ten. In Florida, Byron Donalds won the Republican gubernatorial primary and will face Democrat David Jolly, incumbent Randy Fine defeated Dan Bilzerian, Angie Nixon won her Democratic primary, and Ashley Moody won the Republican Senate primary. In Pennsylvania, a Democrat led by 88 votes with all precincts reporting in a state House district Trump carried by 18 points in 2024, with provisional ballots still to be counted. In South Carolina, Senate candidate Darlene Graham drew attention after misstating the state's population and saying she knew nothing about national security.

Trump voted by mail weeks after calling mail ballots corrupt

tags: politics, elections, legal
sources: @carolinegleich

Palm Beach County records show Donald Trump requested a mail ballot in late July and returned it on August 13 for Florida's Republican primary, weeks after he said mail-in ballots are inherently corrupt and should be eliminated. Utah Lieutenant Governor Deidre Henderson, a Republican, noted that nearly 95 percent of ballots counted in Utah's June primary arrived by mail or drop box, and said the system is safe and secure. Henderson has said she is prepared to sue the Postal Service if the administration's new ballot rule takes effect. The administration is asking the Supreme Court to allow its mail-in voting order to take effect before the midterms after a federal appeals court blocked it.

White House staff departures accelerate ahead of midterms

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A series of White House staffers have left the Trump administration in quick succession. Emily Underwood, a top deputy to Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, announced her exit, following the departure of Caroline Leavitt. Others who have left this year include senior adviser Abigail Jackson, Sonny Joey Nelson, cabinet affairs director Leah Barton, and deputy national security adviser Andy Baker. Republicans on Capitol Hill have expressed concern about the political effect of the war in Iran on the November midterms.

Congressman Randy Fine filmed searching a constituent's mailbox

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

Doorbell camera footage shows Florida Republican Congressman Randy Fine knocking on a home's door and then opening and looking through the resident's mailbox while campaigning. TMZ confirmed the man in the footage is Fine. He does not appear to remove, insert, or tamper with any mail. Interfering with mail is a federal offence, though intent cannot be determined from the footage.

Christian nationalist rally converges on majority-Muslim Dearborn

tags: politics, legal
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Hundreds to thousands of people travelled by motorcycle, RV, and caravan to Dearborn, Michigan, on August 18 for a rally billed as proclaiming Jesus Christ king of the city, in a community that is approximately 54 percent Muslim. Promotional material for the event used AI-generated imagery of a Christian crusader, and organiser figures including Jake Lang were expected to attend. Video from the gathering included overtly Islamophobic language. The event has been compared to the 2017 Charlottesville rally.

US national debt set to pass $40 trillion

tags: markets, economy
sources: @oafnation_actual

The US national debt is likely to surpass $40 trillion this week, months earlier than forecasters had expected. Part of the acceleration is attributed to billions of dollars in lost revenue from President Trump's invalidated tariffs.

Foodborne illness cases in 2026 run five times higher than recent years

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The United States has recorded more than 7,400 cases of foodborne illness so far in 2026, roughly five times the level seen annually between 2021 and 2025. The number of recalls is not unusual, but the illness count is. Public health experts attribute part of the surge to federal funding cuts affecting food inspections and to reduced grants for state and local health departments that conduct traceback investigations.

Forest Service moves to rescind the Roadless Rule entirely

tags: climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins announced on August 18 that the US Forest Service has filed a proposed rule to fully rescind the 2001 Roadless Area Conservation Rule. The rule barred new road construction, reconstruction, and commercial logging across 58.5 million acres of inventoried roadless areas, and was backed by 90 percent of 1.6 million public comments when adopted. The rescission would open 44.7 million acres across 39 states to road building and industrial logging, at a time when the agency's road maintenance backlog stands at $11.2 billion. The affected areas include habitat for wildlife and drinking water sources for 25 million Americans; a Pew poll found 76 percent of American voters, including 76 percent of Trump voters, support keeping the rule.

Mining claims filed in Utah monuments days after Trump shrank their boundaries

tags: climate, legal, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Within a day of a presidential proclamation reducing Bears Ears National Monument by over 90 percent, Kimmerle Mining filed seven mining claims on July 14, 2026, with the San Juan County recorder. Two further claims were filed on August 6 by Craig Rosequist in areas cut from Grand Staircase-Escalante. Under the proclamations themselves, claims cannot be staked until 60 days after the proclamation date, which falls on September 11, and any earlier appropriation vests no rights against the United States. Conservation Lands Foundation CEO Chris Hill said the administration is cutting corners to accelerate development, and the group argues the Bureau of Land Management should reject the claims.

Utah data center water plans draw thousands of formal protests

tags: climate, tech, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Kevin O'Leary is promoting a large AI data center in Box Elder County, Utah, and has said concerns about its water use are overblown, in a state under severe drought and beside a Great Salt Lake with more than half its bed exposed. Thousands of Utahns filed formal protests against water rights applications for the Stratos project; one application was withdrawn and the project footprint was reduced. MIDA, the quasi-state agency that approved Stratos, holds a virtual meeting on Thursday, August 20 at 9 a.m.

Amazon buying and destroying rare books to scan them for AI training

tags: tech, media
sources: @aaronparnas

Reporting by 404 Media describes a previously unreported Amazon operation that acquires large quantities of rare and antique books for AI training data. Reporters placed a tracking device in a rare book and followed it to an Amazon warehouse in Las Vegas, Nevada. Employees there said incoming shipments of printed books have their bindings cut off before being scanned, destroying the physical copies at scale.

Campaign urges Halloween protest against Flock surveillance cameras

tags: surveillance, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

An online campaign is circulating that promotes Halloween as a night to protest automated licence plate and surveillance cameras across the United States. More than 120,000 Flock cameras are in operation nationwide, alongside other surveillance systems. Organisers are encouraging people to demonstrate against the cameras while in costume and masks, following a series of reports about the cameras being used to track individuals.

Strava data exposed routines at US bases across the Middle East

tags: surveillance, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

More than 1,300 Strava users publicly exposed activity routines at United States military bases across the Middle East. The exposed fitness tracking data reveals patterns of movement around the installations.

Lavrov says Russia and North Korea are building a new world order

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Russia and North Korea are building what he called a new and righteous world order. The remarks point to deepening ties between the two governments.

Trump drill cuts reshape the US-South Korea alliance

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Reductions to joint military exercises ordered under President Trump have altered the character of the United States alliance with South Korea. The changes mark a shift in how the two militaries train and coordinate.

Palm Beach County clerk Mike Caruso arrested on child molestation charge

tags: legal, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Mike Caruso, the county clerk in Palm Beach County, Florida, has been arrested on a charge of child molestation.

Army veteran who shot burglar faces $10 million civil trial

tags: legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

An Army veteran who shot a man later convicted of burglary is facing a civil trial seeking $10 million in damages. The case is proceeding in Portland.

Marine Corps orders 10 mobile counter-drone vehicles

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Marine Corps is purchasing 10 Tempest counter-drone vehicles designed for shoot-and-scoot operation. The mobile systems are intended to counter unmanned aerial threats.

Army drops planned minimum test score for ROTC cadets

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Army has scrapped a planned rule that would have set a minimum test score for incoming ROTC cadets. The requirement will not take effect.

US military-funded research underpins China's robot dog industry

tags: tech, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Technology developed with United States military funding helped pioneer the quadruped robots behind China's rapidly growing robot dog industry. The research pathway links American defence investment to a now-booming Chinese manufacturing sector.

Scrutiny grows over presidential aide Natalie Harp's conduct

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

CNN reported that Natalie Harp, a 35-year-old aide to President Trump, climbed into an SUV in the presidential motorcade in 2023 after being told there was no seat for her, following a shouting match. Harp's brother, from whom she is now estranged, told CNN he believes she has an unhealthy obsession with the president and said he hopes she reconsiders. The New York Times reported a newly unearthed handwritten note from Harp to Trump apologising for being a possible embarrassment and describing lost sleep and missed meals, signed "with all my heart, Natalie". Harp has more direct access to the president than most staff.
